I found one bug in the uncommitted change, `clinic/evaluate.py`, at line 15.

The cross-validation splits by visit, not by patient. `StratifiedKFold` ignores `patient_id`. A data file like this has several visits per patient with repeated per-patient features (age, `n_chronic`). So the same patient can end up in both the training and test folds. The model can then memorize those patients, and the reported PR-AUC will be higher than it would be on new patients.

The fix is to use `StratifiedGroupKFold` with `groups=df["patient_id"]`, and pass `groups` to `cv.split`.

I read the file and the data module's docstring but didn't run anything. I found nothing else wrong.

findings.summary: StratifiedKFold splits at the visit level, but rows from the same patient_id share per-patient features and appear across many visits, so the same patient lands in both train and test folds (group leakage).
findings.failure_scenario: A patient with 4 visits has some visits in training and others in the test fold. The model memorizes the repeated age/n_chronic values and their outcome, so the reported PR-AUC is inflated compared with performance on new patients. Fix: use StratifiedGroupKFold (or GroupKFold) with groups=df['patient_id'] and pass groups to cv.split.
findings.short_summary: CV splits by visit, leaking patients across folds
